title: Pushforward along a closed immersion of the products with the powers of an extended ideal
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and let $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ be the image of $i^*\mathcal I\to i^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Z$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal, def-pc-module-pullback]. Products $\mathcal K\mathcal F$ of a quasi-coherent ideal and a module, the powers $\mathcal K^n$ and the quotients $\mathcal F/\mathcal K\mathcal F$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). (1) $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_Z$, and for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $i^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathcal J(U))$, one has $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)(i^{-1}U)=\mathcal I(U)\cdot(R/\mathcal J(U))$, the image of $\mathcal I(U)$. (2) For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every $n\ge1$, $i_*\big((\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G\big)=\mathcal I^n\,(i_*\mathcal G)$ as sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules of $i_*\mathcal G$. (3) Consequently, for the quotient map $q:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G$, the map $i_*q$ induces an isomorphism $i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)\to i_*\big(\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G\big)$, natural in $\mathcal G$ and compatible, for $m\ge n$, with the quotient maps from level $m$ to level $n$.

proof.text: (Affine opens of $X$.) Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ be an affine open [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; the affine opens of $X$ form a basis of its topology. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1) the open subscheme $i^{-1}(V)$ of $Z$ is affine and $i^\sharp_V:R=\mathcal O_X(V)\to\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)$ is surjective; its kernel is $\mathcal J(V)$ by the definition of the ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. So $i^\sharp_V$ induces a ring isomorphism $\bar R:=R/\mathcal J(V)\cong\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)$, and $i^{-1}(V)\to V$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\bar R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. For an $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H$, the pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback] has sections $(i_*\mathcal H)(W)=\mathcal H(i^{-1}W)$ for every open $W\subseteq X$, with restriction maps those of $\mathcal H$ and $a\in\mathcal O_X(W)$ acting as $i^\sharp_W(a)$; in particular $(i_*\mathcal H)(V)$ is the $\bar R$-module $\mathcal H(i^{-1}V)$ viewed as an $R$-module through $R\to\bar R$, and $i_*$ of a sub-$\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal H'\subseteq\mathcal H$ is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal H'(i^{-1}W)$ of $i_*\mathcal H$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01QO (morphisms-lemma-closed-immersion), (1)=>(2)/(3): closed immersions are affine-locally Spec of quotients

proof.text: (Part (1).) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1) to the morphism $f=i:Z\to X$ and the quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$: the image $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z$ of $i^*\mathcal I\to i^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Z$ (the ideal of [def-nagata-extended-ideal]) is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_Z$, and for the affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $X$ and the affine open $i^{-1}(V)\subseteq i^{-1}(V)$ of $Z$ (step 1), $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)(i^{-1}V)$ is the ideal of $\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)$ generated by $i^\sharp_V(\mathcal I(V))$. Since $i^\sharp_V$ is a surjective ring map (step 1), $i^\sharp_V(\mathcal I(V))$ is already an ideal; under $\mathcal O_Z(i^{-1}V)\cong\bar R=R/\mathcal J(V)$ it is the image $\mathcal I(V)\cdot\bar R$ of $\mathcal I(V)$. This is (1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback), affine description of f^{-1}I O_X, specialized to a closed immersion

proof.text: (Quasi-coherence of the sheaves in (2), (3).) Fix a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ [pqf-def-coherent] and $n\ge1$, and put $\mathcal K=(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n$, products, powers and quotients as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1) on $Z$ (the ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z$ is quasi-coherent by step 2), $\mathcal K$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_Z$ and $\mathcal K\mathcal G$, $\mathcal G/\mathcal K\mathcal G$ are quasi-coherent; on $X$, $\mathcal I^n$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-pushforward-annihilated] (1), $i_*\mathcal G$ and $i_*(\mathcal G/\mathcal K\mathcal G)$ are quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules; hence, by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1) on $X$ (ideal $\mathcal I^n$, module $i_*\mathcal G$), so are $\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)$ and $i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)$. By step 1, $i_*(\mathcal K\mathcal G)$ is the sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $W\mapsto(\mathcal K\mathcal G)(i^{-1}W)$ of $i_*\mathcal G$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 01QY (morphisms-lemma-i-star-equivalence): i_* of a quasi-coherent module along a closed immersion is quasi-coherent

proof.text: (Sections over an affine open.) Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ be an affine open of $X$, $\bar R=R/\mathcal J(V)$, $\mathfrak a=\mathcal I(V)$ and $M=\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)=(i_*\mathcal G)(V)$, a $\bar R$-module and, through $R\to\bar R$, an $R$-module (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2) on $Z$ at the affine open $i^{-1}(V)$: $\mathcal K(i^{-1}V)=((\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)(i^{-1}V))^n=(\mathfrak a\bar R)^n$ (step 2), $(\mathcal K\mathcal G)(i^{-1}V)=(\mathfrak a\bar R)^nM$, and $q_{i^{-1}V}:M\to(\mathcal G/\mathcal K\mathcal G)(i^{-1}V)$ is surjective with kernel $(\mathfrak a\bar R)^nM$, where $q:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/\mathcal K\mathcal G$ is the quotient map. By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2) on $X$ at $V$, for the quasi-coherent module $i_*\mathcal G$ (step 3): $\mathcal I^n(V)=\mathfrak a^n$, $(\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G))(V)=\mathfrak a^nM$, and $p_V:M\to(i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G)(V)$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak a^nM$, where $p:i_*\mathcal G\to i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^n i_*\mathcal G$ is the quotient map.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I8 (schemes-lemma-widetilde-constructions) and Lemma 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent), through the cited node

proof.text: (A module identity.) Let $\pi:R\to\bar R$ be a surjective ring map, $\mathfrak a\subseteq R$ an ideal, $M$ a $\bar R$-module regarded as an $R$-module through $\pi$, and $n\ge1$. Then $(\mathfrak a\bar R)^nM=\mathfrak a^nM$. Indeed $\mathfrak a\bar R=\pi(\mathfrak a)$ ($\pi$ surjective), and $\pi(\mathfrak a)^n$ is generated by the products $\pi(a_1)\cdots\pi(a_n)=\pi(a_1\cdots a_n)$, so $(\mathfrak a\bar R)^n=\pi(\mathfrak a^n)$; and $\pi(\mathfrak a^n)M$ is generated by the elements $\pi(b)m=bm$, $b\in\mathfrak a^n$, $m\in M$, i.e. equals $\mathfrak a^nM$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A, lines 6961-6968 (used without mention)

proof.text: (Part (2).) By steps 4 and 5, $(i_*(\mathcal K\mathcal G))(V)=(\mathcal K\mathcal G)(i^{-1}V)=(\mathfrak a\bar R)^nM=\mathfrak a^nM=(\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G))(V)$ inside $(i_*\mathcal G)(V)=M$, for every affine open $V$ of $X$. Both $i_*(\mathcal K\mathcal G)$ (step 3) and $\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)$ are sub-$\mathcal O_X$-modules of $i_*\mathcal G$, and sub-sheaves agreeing on a basis are equal: for an open $W$ and $s\in(i_*(\mathcal K\mathcal G))(W)$, cover $W$ by affine opens $V_k$; then $s|_{V_k}\in(\mathcal I^n i_*\mathcal G)(V_k)$, these restrictions agree on overlaps and glue (the subsheaf is a sheaf) to $t\in(\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G)(W)$ with $t|_{V_k}=s|_{V_k}$, so $t=s$ in $i_*\mathcal G$; symmetrically. Hence $i_*((\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G)=\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A, lines 6961-6968 (used without mention)

proof.text: (The map of (3).) Let $\iota:\mathcal K\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ be the inclusion; $q\circ\iota=0$ since $q$ is the cokernel of $\iota$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). As $i_*$ is a functor of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], $i_*q\circ i_*\iota=0$, and by step 6 $i_*\iota$ is the inclusion $\mathcal I^n(i_*\mathcal G)\subseteq i_*\mathcal G$. By the universal property of the cokernel $p$ there is a unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\rho_{\mathcal G}:i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G\to i_*(\mathcal G/\mathcal K\mathcal G)$ with $\rho_{\mathcal G}\circ p=i_*q$; this is the map induced by $i_*q$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A, lines 6961-6968 (used without mention)

proof.text: ($\rho_{\mathcal G}$ is an isomorphism.) On an affine open $V$ of $X$ (notation of step 4): $(i_*q)_V=q_{i^{-1}V}:M\to(\mathcal G/\mathcal K\mathcal G)(i^{-1}V)$ is surjective with kernel $(\mathfrak a\bar R)^nM=\mathfrak a^nM$ (steps 4, 5), and $p_V$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak a^nM$ (step 4); since $\rho_{\mathcal G,V}\circ p_V=q_{i^{-1}V}$, $\rho_{\mathcal G,V}$ is bijective. A morphism of sheaves bijective on every open of a basis is an isomorphism: for an open $W$ covered by affine opens $V_k$, if $\rho_W(s)=0$ then $\rho_{V_k}(s|_{V_k})=0$, so $s|_{V_k}=0$ for all $k$ and $s=0$; for $t$ in the target over $W$ let $s_k$ be the preimage of $t|_{V_k}$; on an affine open $V'\subseteq V_k\cap V_l$ both $s_k|_{V'}$ and $s_l|_{V'}$ map to $t|_{V'}$, so they agree, hence $s_k,s_l$ agree on $V_k\cap V_l$ and glue to $s$ with $\rho_W(s)|_{V_k}=t|_{V_k}$, i.e. $\rho_W(s)=t$. So $\rho_{\mathcal G}$ is bijective on all opens, an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 088A, lines 6961-6968 (used without mention)

proof.text: (Naturality and compatibility with the levels.) Let $u:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ be $\mathcal O_Z$-linear between quasi-coherent modules. As $u(as)=au(s)$, $u$ maps the image of $\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ into that of $\mathcal K\otimes\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G'$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0), so it induces $\bar u$ with $\bar u\circ q=q'\circ u$; likewise $i_*u$ induces $\bar u'$ on $i_*\mathcal G/\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G$ with $\bar u'\circ p=p'\circ i_*u$. Then $i_*\bar u\circ\rho_{\mathcal G}\circ p=i_*(\bar u\circ q)=i_*(q'\circ u)=\rho_{\mathcal G'}\circ p'\circ i_*u=\rho_{\mathcal G'}\circ\bar u'\circ p$, and $p$ is an epimorphism, so $i_*\bar u\circ\rho_{\mathcal G}=\rho_{\mathcal G'}\circ\bar u'$. For $m\ge n$: $\mathcal L^{k+1}=\mathcal L\cdot\mathcal L^k\subseteq\mathcal L^k$ for an ideal $\mathcal L$ (as $\mathcal L^k$ is an ideal), so $(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^m\mathcal G\subseteq(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G$ and $\mathcal I^mi_*\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal I^ni_*\mathcal G$; the quotient maps $\theta:\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^m\mathcal G\to\mathcal G/(\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z)^n\mathcal G$ and $\theta'$ on the $i_*\mathcal G$ side satisfy $\theta\circ q_m=q_n$, $\theta'\circ p_m=p_n$, so $i_*\theta\circ\rho^m_{\mathcal G}\circ p_m=i_*q_n=\rho^n_{\mathcal G}\circ p_n=\rho^n_{\mathcal G}\circ\theta'\circ p_m$, and $i_*\theta\circ\rho^m_{\mathcal G}=\rho^n_{\mathcal G}\circ\theta'$ since $p_m$ is an epimorphism. This is (3).
